criteria.quote: Three minds can make Exeggutor unable to move.
criteria.revision: Make the first line more specific and paradoxical: "Exeggutor can be unable to move simply because its three heads want different directions."

criteria.quote: Each head has its own thoughts, so one body carries three separate wills.
What happens when Exeggutor's three heads disagree?
criteria.revision: Make the question focus on the unresolved contradiction: "If the heads can use telepathy to discuss plans, why do different directions still leave Exeggutor unable to move?"

criteria.quote: They use telepathy to discuss plans before choosing one shared direction.
criteria.revision: Make the final escalation more concrete by specifying what cooperation produces: "When they work together, each head fires off psychokinetic energy, tripling their power."

criteria.quote: When they work together, the same three heads can release powerful psychic energy.
criteria.revision: Sharpen the reversal with the documented mechanism: "The heads that can stop Exeggutor from moving can also fire psychokinetic energy together, tripling its power."

criteria.quote: Three minds can make Exeggutor unable to move.
criteria.revision: Replace the first scene's restatement with a new concrete detail: "Its cries are very noisy because each head thinks about whatever it likes." Keep the later scene as the movement reveal.

criteria.quote: Conflicting directions stop Exeggutor completely, but cooperation lets its heads unleash powerful psychic energy.
criteria.revision: End on the stronger documented contrast: "Different directions leave Exeggutor unable to move—but when the heads work together, their psychokinetic energy triples in power."

criteria.quote: Teamwork, or one mind per body?
criteria.revision: Use a genuine interpretive split grounded in the entries: "Is Exeggutor best understood as three independent minds—or one Pokémon whose power depends on cooperation?"
